description: Turns a phasor into standard waveforms, unipolar in one column and bipolar in the other; nothing here is anti-aliased, so audio-rate use is for phase distortion

inputs.text: The phasor being converted, 0-10V; voltages outside that range wrap back into it

outputs.text: A sine wave across one cycle of the input phasor, 0-10V
A triangle across one cycle of the input phasor, 0-10V
A rising sawtooth across one cycle of the input phasor, 0-10V; with an ordinary phasor patched in, this matches the input
A falling sawtooth across one cycle of the input phasor, 0-10V
10V through the first half of the input phasor's cycle and 0V through the second
A sine wave across one cycle of the input phasor, -5V to +5V
A triangle across one cycle of the input phasor, -5V to +5V
A rising sawtooth across one cycle of the input phasor, -5V to +5V
A falling sawtooth across one cycle of the input phasor, -5V to +5V
5V through the first half of the input phasor's cycle and -5V through the second

notes: a phasor drives this, not a clock: a ramp rising from 0V to 10V once per cycle, from Phasor Generator, Clock to Phasor or an LFO's saw output. Nothing moves here until one is patched in.
